subcategory_text: Potential problematic data actions and associated problems are identified.
informative_references: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5: RA-3, SI-4 (System Monitoring)
GDPR Art. 35(7)(c) (DPIA — assessment of risks to rights and freedoms)
Aligned with NIST CSF 2.0 ID.RA-04 (potential threats catalogued)
implementation_examples: Conduct scenario analysis to identify potentially problematic data actions (e.g., function creep, unanticipated secondary uses, opaque processing) and the associated problems they would create for individuals
Capture each problematic action together with its problem statement so that downstream prioritisation and treatment decisions are grounded
Update the set as new data actions are onboarded and as new research findings emerge
assessment_objectives: Determine whether problematic data actions are identified per processing activity
Determine whether the problems they would create for individuals are documented
Determine whether the set is updated on onboarding of new data actions
Determine whether the set is informed by external research and incident learnings
